notes.b1/j1/B-r1: Counts 5-7-5 (sun gone from the street / a veil of ice up there still / burning pearl and rose); the street-to-sky cut is strong and nacreous clouds are evoked without being named, though 'veil' and 'pearl' are slightly familiar.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Counts 5-7-5 (Mother-of-pearl veils / nacreous light at dusk, slow / fire on frozen air); accurately names nacreous clouds and the ice-fire contrast, but mother-of-pearl is the stock phrase and the middle line is padded.
notes.b1/j1/B-r2: Counts 5-7-5 (Winter dusk, sun gone / a veil too high for the dark / holds mother-of-pearl); the idea of a cloud too high for the darkness is accurate to polar stratospheric clouds and gives the poem its turn.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Counts 4-7-5 (Nacreous glow = 4), so the opening line misses the form, and 'the sky holds its breath' is a stock closer.
notes.b1/j2/B-r2: Syllables 5-7-5 (Win-ter dusk sun gone / a veil too high for the dark / holds moth-er-of-pearl); the veil too high for the dark accurately evokes nacreous clouds lit after sunset, though the last line is a stock term.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: Syllables 4-7-5 (Na-cre-ous glow = 4), so the first line is short; names nacreous and mother-of-pearl but the sky holds its breath is cliche and the images stay abstract.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: Syllables 5-7-5 (fire may count as 2, making line 3 a 6); fire on frozen air is a strong image, but nacreous light at dusk, slow is clotted and repeats the mother-of-pearl idea.
notes.b1/j2/B-r1: Syllables 5-7-5 (sun gone from the street / a veil of ice up there still / burning pearl and rose); street-level vantage, ice crystals and still burning color evoke polar stratospheric clouds without naming them.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Counts 4-7-5 (Na-cre-ous glow = 4), so line one is short, and 'holds its breath' is stock.
notes.b1/j3/B-r2: 5-7-5 (Win-ter dusk sun gone / a veil too high for the dark / holds moth-er-of-pearl); the high veil against the dark is a real turn and evokes polar stratospheric clouds accurately.
notes.b1/j3/B-r1: 5-7-5 (sun gone from the street / a veil of ice up there still / burning pearl and rose); concrete street-to-sky contrast and ice-crystal accuracy, slightly less of a closing turn.
notes.b1/j3/A-r1: 5-7-5 or 5-7-6 depending on 'fire' (Moth-er-of-pearl veils / na-cre-ous light at dusk slow / fire on fro-zen air); names nacreous and the frozen air but the lines are stacked and the break at 'slow' is awkward.
notes.b2/j1/B-r3: Counts 5-7-5 (cloud lens on the ridge / all the wind pours through it still / and the smell of snow); lenticular cloud evoked with a fresh smell-of-snow turn, though 'lens' is unnamed as rare.
notes.b2/j1/A-r3: Counts 5-7-5 (na-cre-ous glow burns / in the long dark before dawn / mother-of-pearl sky); accurate polar stratospheric nacreous cloud, but mother-of-pearl is the stock descriptor and the ending just restates.
notes.b2/j1/B-r4: Counts 5-7-5 (cold cup on the sill / the lens cloud over the ridge / holds still, wind running); the domestic cup against the still lens cloud is a nice cut, though the link is loose.
notes.b2/j1/A-r4: Counts 6-7-5 (moth-er-of-pearl sheets is 6), so form slips; mother-of-pearl and nacreous together are redundant and the last line is vague.
notes.b2/j2/B-r4: 5-7-5 (Cold cup on the sill=5; the lens cloud over the ridge=7; holds still, wind running=5); the cup on the sill is a surprising cut and the stillness-with-wind paradox is true to lenticulars, though the link between cup and cloud is loose.
notes.b2/j2/A-r4: 5-7-5 (Mother-of-pearl sheets=5; nacreous light on cold air=7 with nacreous as 3; dawn the sky holds, brief=5); accurate to nacreous clouds but the last line is clumsy and the phrasing is stock.
notes.b2/j2/A-r3: 5-7-5 (Nacreous glow burns=5; in the long dark before dawn=7; mother-of-pearl sky=5); evocative of polar stratospheric clouds glowing before dawn, but nacreous and mother-of-pearl say the same thing twice.
notes.b2/j2/B-r3: 5-7-5 (Cloud lens on the ridge=5; all the wind pours through it, still=7; and the smell of snow=5); lenticular is accurately evoked, and the closing smell of snow adds a new sense and a quiet turn.
notes.b2/j3/A-r4: Counts 5-7-5 (Mother-of-pearl sheets 5; na-cre-ous light on cold air 7; dawn the sky holds, brief 5); accurate nacreous clouds but stock 'mother-of-pearl' and a slightly muddled last line.
notes.b2/j3/B-r4: Counts 5-7-5 (Cold cup on the sill 5; the lens cloud over the ridge 7; holds still, wind running 5); lenticular cloud is evoked but the cup image is disconnected and the ending is cryptic.
notes.b2/j3/B-r3: Counts 5-7-5 (Cloud lens on the ridge 5; all the wind pours through it, still 7; and the smell of snow 5); the lenticular cloud holding still while wind pours through it is true and the smell of snow is a fresh turn.
notes.b2/j3/A-r3: Counts 5-7-5 (Nacreous glow burns 5; in the long dark before dawn 7; mother-of-pearl sky 5); accurate to polar stratospheric clouds but 'glow burns' is imprecise and the close is stock phrasing.
